reviewed.by: ROUND 4 — 5 gate rounds run (argument, orthodoxy x3, neutrality x2, citations). NOT YET RE-GATED. STANDING CONSTRAINTS, do not undo: (1) The Daniel 4:34 'everlasting dominion' parallel is an ECHO, not a proof, and the two dim lines saying so are load-bearing -- Dan 7:18 and 7:27 give the saints an everlasting kingdom, so the phrase is NOT a God-only predicate and 'not a creature promoted' is answered in one line without them. ev-m-titles.html's own verdict is 'the clouds are the stronger half'. (2) Never claim pelach/'serve' is used only of God (retired: tools/retired-claims.json, pelach-only-to-God; Dan 3:12/14/18 use it of Nebuchadnezzar's gods), and keep the gold OFF 'should serve him' -- the highlight rebuilt that retired argument visually in round 1. (3) Never date Daniel; library/daniel70.html names the Maccabean dating as the majority academic view. 'Centuries before that trial' is true on both datings -- preserve verbatim. (4) The scene-12 hedge 'Not the only Jewish reading' is required: the earliest surviving reading of Daniel 7 is INSIDE Daniel 7 (the interpreting angel at 7:18/22/27 reads the figure corporately), and 4 Ezra is c. AD 90-100, later than Jesus. Do not restore 'the oldest Jewish readings'. (5) 'always' in 'Those clouds were always his' defuses the harpagmos register -- never trade it for 'are' or 'became'. (6) 'because it was' must appear on the CARD, not only the voiceover; its absence there was a round-3 DRIFT. Deity-of-Christ tier: needs apologia-orthodoxy + apologia-neutrality on THIS text before any stamp.

voiceover: A prisoner stood before the high priest. The witnesses had contradicted each other and the case was falling apart. Then the high priest asked him directly: are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? He answered: I am, and you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of heaven. He did not invent that language. He was fusing two texts at once — Daniel 7 and Psalm 110. Centuries before that trial, the book of Daniel records a vision: with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man. In the Hebrew Bible, that is God's own imagery. He makes the clouds his chariot, says Psalm 104. The LORD is riding on a swift cloud, says Isaiah. And Daniel watches someone else arrive that way. Daniel does not tell us who he is. The New Testament does: not a second God, and not a creature — the Son is God, and God is one. Then Daniel says what the figure receives: dominion and glory and a kingdom, and all peoples, nations, and languages serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion. And that phrase — an everlasting dominion — is word for word what the book of Daniel says of the Most High himself. Daniel promises the saints a lasting kingdom too, so the phrase is the echo, not the proof. The clouds are the proof. And on Christian terms this is not a creature promoted: what the Son receives as man, he never lacked as God — truly God and truly man. Jewish readers were already taking that figure as an individual, a coming messiah. Not the only reading of Daniel's vision, but it was there, and it was Jewish. Jesus was not inventing a reading. He was claiming one. Son of Man was his own name for himself, about eighty times in the Gospels, almost always on his own lips. And on the night it mattered most, he took the one Daniel saw on the clouds and said: that is me. The high priest did not ask what he meant. He tore his robes and called it blasphemy. No single title settles the question on its own, and specialists still argue over this one. The case is cumulative. But this is the language Israel reserved for her God, and Jesus took it as his own — because it was. Those clouds were always his.
